la:noun:conexio.html:
cōnexĭo (conn-), ōnis, f.
conecto
, t. t.
A binding together, close union, etc.: scutorum, armorum (in a testudo),; . —
Esp.
An organic union; cf. Paul. ex Müll.: animae et corporis nostri,.—
In philos. lang. (almost confined to Quint.), a conclusion, a logical sequence, ; ; ; 22 sq.—*
In gram., a syllable, P.

la:noun:conexum.gloss: a proposition that follows necessarily, a necessary consequence, a logical entailment, an inevitable inference
senses: a proposition that follows necessarily, a necessary consequence, a logical entailment, an inevitable inference

la:verb:conecto.html:
cōnecto (less correctly, connecto, v. Ritschl, Opusc. II. 448 sq.; ), nexŭi, nexum, 3, v. a.
necto
,
to tie, bind, fasten, or join together, to connect, entwine, link together (class.; most freq. in part. pass. and the trop. signif.); constr. with cum, inter se, the dat., or absol.
Lit.: id (palliolum) conexum in umero laevo,folded, gathered,: omnia inter se conexa et apta,: omnia omnimodis,: terrestria membra marinis,; ; : illae (apes) pedibus conexae ad limina pendent,; cf. : crines,: nodos,: bracchia in genibus digitis conexa tenere,: naves validis utrimque trabibus,: Mosellam atque Ararim facta inter utrumque fossa,; cf.: Adiabenis conectuntur Carduchi,: lata alvus (navium) sine vinculo aeris aut ferri conexa,: ferreae laminae serie inter se conexae,.—
Trop.
In gen.: amicitia cum voluptate conectitur,; : ita sunt inter se conexa et indiscreta omnia,; ; cf. * : membra historiae,: quod discrimini patris filiam conectebat,to implicate, involve,; cf. : causam dolori meo,; .—
Esp.,
In discourse, to connect with what precedes, join to, etc.: facilius est enim apta dissolvere quam dissipata conectere,: illud non est in uno verbo translato, sed ex pluribus continuatis conectitur,: inter se pleraque conexa et apta,; : verba lyrae conectere, : carmina secum gracili filo,: res ac verba,; : conexa oratio (opp. interrupta),: aliam majorem insaniam,to join to,; hence also: versus orationesque ejus, to quote, cite, Treb. Gall. 11 fin.—
In philos. lang., = concludo, to annex or subjoin a logical conclusion: si enim est verum, quod ita conectitur: si quis, etc. ... illud quoque verum est, etc.,; : omne, quod ipsum ex se conexum sit (e. g. si lucet, lucet) verum esse, etc.,.—Hence, cō-nexus, a, um, P. a., = conjunctus, connected, joined, cohering together with something (very rare): sive aliud quid vis potius conexius (quam animus) ei (sc. corpori) fingere,: Silanum per adfinitatem conexum Germanico,; so also without affinitas, of relationship: Caesari,; 4, 66: insequitur magno jam tunc conexus amore Patroclus,.—
In time, immediately following: conexi his funeribus dies,.—Hence, subst.: cōnexum (conn-), i, a necessary consequence, inevitable inference: ipsa ratio conexi, cum concesseris superius, cogit inferius concedere,: primumque quod est in conexo ... necessarium est,; cf. : quod Graeci συνημμένον ἀξίωμα dicunt, alii nostrorum conjunctum, alii conexum dixerunt, ; cf. the context.—And adv.: cōnexē (conn-), in connection, connectedly: dicere aliquid,.

,
